entries.sense_en: searching for; hunting for

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and neutral; 'in quest of' is literary and suggests a long, determined search.
Informal; stresses active, eager searching.
synonyms.example: on the hunt for a bargain

entries.sense_en: walked around an area again and again to guard it or watch for danger

synonyms.nuance: Protects a place, but you can do it standing still; patrol always means moving around.
Moves quietly, often with bad or hunting intent; patrol is official and protective.

entries.sense_en: very steep, like the edge of a cliff

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for any sharp slope; precipitous suggests a dangerous drop.
Almost vertical, like a wall of rock; used for cliffs and drops.

entries.sense_en: gave shelter to; had living in it

synonyms.nuance: Protects from danger or weather, usually with kind intent.
Keeps out of sight; harbour is often used for criminals or bad feelings.
Plain, general word; harbour suggests something living or hidden inside.

entries.tip_ko: harbour grudges처럼 감정을 '품다'의 뜻으로도 자주 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: took something away by force or great effort

synonyms.nuance: Grab suddenly and firmly; wrest suggests a struggle against someone holding on.
A quick, sudden grab, not a long struggle.
Neutral and positive; carries no sense of force or unfairness.

entries.tip_ko: 발음할 때 w는 소리 나지 않습니다(/rɛst/).

entries.sense_en: accepted something without protest, even though unwilling

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; does not imply reluctance.
Gives in to a stronger power; more humbling than acquiesce.
Follows a rule or order; acquiesce is about quiet agreement without arguing.

entries.tip_ko: 'in the judgment'처럼 acquiesce in/to와 함께 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a violent fight or clash that breaks the peace

synonyms.nuance: Common word for a rough, noisy fight, often in a bar.
Smaller, shorter, less serious than an affray.
A noisy quarrel or fight; a bit formal, stresses the uproar.

entries.sense_en: filled (a relationship) with bitterness and resentment

synonyms.nuance: Stronger, figurative: ruins a relationship completely.
Makes something gradually unpleasant; milder than embitter.

entries.tip_ko: bitter(쓴)에서 나온 말로, 마음이 '쓰게' 변한다는 이미지입니다.

entries.sense_en: a long, bitter quarrel between two people or families

synonyms.nuance: Any angry argument, can be brief; a feud lasts for years or generations.
A feud driven by revenge, often for a past wrong.
Competition between equals, not necessarily hatred.

entries.sense_en: hated very strongly

synonyms.nuance: Basic, strong word; can be used lightly for foods or chores.
Even stronger, with disgust.
Hate mixed with looking down on someone as worthless.

entries.sense_en: moving around quietly, looking for a chance to steal or attack

synonyms.nuance: Stays hidden and waits in one place; prowl keeps moving.
Moves secretly out of guilt or fear, not just hunting.
Wanders freely with no bad intent.

entries.sense_en: an animal or person that is being hunted

synonyms.nuance: An animal hunted by a predator for food; quarry is what a human hunter pursues.
Wild animals hunted for sport or food, as a group.
Anything aimed at; not limited to hunting.

entries.sense_en: in the habit of doing something

synonyms.nuance: Used to something; more neutral and modern.
Everyday form: 'used to sleep'.

entries.tip_ko: won't(will not)와 발음·철자가 비슷하니 혼동하지 마세요.

entries.sense_en: a hidden place from which people wait to watch or attack

synonyms.nuance: A device or plan that catches someone; ambush is a hidden waiting position.
Any hiding place, not necessarily for attacking.

entries.sense_en: making a shrill, high, piercing sound
entries.sense_ko: 날카롭고 높은 소리를 내다 (바람 소리 등)

synonyms.nuance: A sudden, loud, high cry, usually from a person.
A clear high sound, less harsh.
A long, low-to-high wail, like wind or wolves.

entries.sense_en: a person who roams around looking for things to steal or attack

synonyms.nuance: Makes a quick, planned attack on a place.
An armed robber, often in groups on the road.
Steals during a disaster or war, from already damaged places.

entries.sense_en: calmly and deliberately, without anger or passion

synonyms.nuance: On purpose; does not imply cruelty.
Without pity, but may be done in anger.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 살인 같은 잔인한 행위와 함께 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: before

synonyms.nuance: The normal word today; ere is old-fashioned and poetic.
Marks the point at which something stops; ere only ever means 'before' and never 'up to a time'.

entries.sense_en: held tightly so that one cannot move

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for held in place by weight or force.
Unable to escape, but not necessarily held down by a weight.
Tied with rope or chains.

entries.sense_en: unable to feel anything

synonyms.nuance: Informal: 'my leg went dead' means no feeling for a while.
Prickly feeling as sensation returns, not total lack of feeling.

entries.sense_en: a difficult, unfortunate situation

synonyms.nuance: A tricky situation that is hard to get out of, often puzzling.
General and mild.
A choice between two bad options.

entries.sense_en: strong annoyance from being unable to change something

synonyms.nuance: Mild irritation.
Feeling blocked from reaching a goal.
Between annoyance and anger; often from repeated small things.

entries.sense_en: a mixture of different things

synonyms.nuance: General word for things combined.
synonyms.example: a mixture of fear and joy

synonyms.nuance: A messy, disordered mix.
Casual, short form.

entries.sense_en: caught in a trap

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for catching an animal or person.
More formal; often figurative, catching someone in a trick.

entries.sense_en: answered back quickly and sharply

synonyms.nuance: Neutral answer.
Answers angrily and suddenly.
Strikes back, usually with actions, not just words.

entries.sense_en: only to follow polite custom, not because one means it

synonyms.nuance: To look proper to others.
Done because rules require it.

entries.sense_en: words of sympathy for someone who has lost a family member

synonyms.nuance: Feeling sorry for any trouble.
Polite greetings, not sorrow.

entries.sense_en: a drink, taken in one swallow or so

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for any liquid.
Informal gulp from a bottle.
A big, quick swallow.

entries.sense_en: a heavy, tired, weak feeling

synonyms.nuance: Tiredness from effort.
Lack of energy, sometimes from illness.
Deep tiredness from effort or illness; common in medical use.

entries.sense_en: a formal agreement between people

synonyms.nuance: General word.
Serious agreement, often between groups or nations.
Informal; often business.

entries.sense_en: to end an old quarrel and put it in the past

synonyms.nuance: Plain, general.
Informal, used for friends and couples.

entries.tip_ko: bury는 여기서 '(다툼을) 묻어 두다, 잊다'라는 뜻이며, 같은 뜻의 관용 표현으로 bury the hatchet이 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: talk fast and noisily, often about gossip

synonyms.nuance: Fast, light talk; friendly.
Talk that is hard to follow.
Talk about other people's private lives.

entries.sense_en: coming in short bursts, not steady

synonyms.nuance: Not steady or even.
Starts and stops repeatedly; more technical.
Happening at scattered times.

entries.sense_en: help given to someone in trouble

synonyms.nuance: Help, often official or organised.
Help that eases suffering.
Saving from immediate danger.

entries.sense_en: a shout to attract attention

synonyms.nuance: General loud call.
Harsh, often angry or excited.
Call out to get attention from far away.

entries.sense_en: extremely annoying; cursed

synonyms.nuance: Strong curse word for something annoying.
Miserable or bad.
Very bad in a general way.

entries.sense_en: in a rough, dry voice

synonyms.nuance: Low and rough, sometimes attractive.
Rough and unfriendly in manner.
Unpleasant or cruel in tone.

entries.sense_en: so upset that one loses self-control

synonyms.nuance: Frightened and losing courage.
Upset by a shock; milder.
Informal: made nervous.
